descriptors.definition: An intangible asset is carried at a revalued amount representing its fair value at the date of revaluation less subsequent amortisation and impairment losses. Fair value must be determined by reference to an active market, and applying this model requires revaluing all other assets in the same class.
inclusion: Intangible assets with active markets
Assets received via government grant at nominal amounts
exclusion: Initial recognition of intangible assets at non-cost amounts
nearby_distinctions: Unlike the cost model which uses historical cost less accumulated depreciation and impairment, the revaluation model uses fair value based on active markets.

descriptors.definition: Useful life defines the period over which an intangible asset is expected to generate economic benefits or the number of production units constituting that life. Entities must assess whether this life is finite or indefinite based on relevant technical, commercial, and legal factors.
inclusion: Expected usage and product life cycles
Legal, regulatory, or contractual limits
exclusion: Planned future expenditures exceeding standard maintenance requirements
nearby_distinctions: Finite useful lives trigger mandatory systematic amortisation, whereas indefinite useful lives require annual impairment testing without amortisation.

descriptors.concept_name: Intangible Assets With Finite Useful Lives
descriptors.definition: Intangible assets with finite useful lives are subject to systematic allocation of their depreciable amount over their operational lifespan. Their residual value is presumed to be zero unless a third-party purchase commitment exists or an active market guarantees realizable value.
inclusion: Assets with limited periods of economic benefit
Assets with third-party purchase commitments
exclusion: Assets assessed to have indefinite useful lives
nearby_distinctions: Finite life assets undergo regular amortisation over time, distinguishing them from indefinite life assets which are tested solely for impairment.

descriptors.concept_name: Depreciable amount to be amortised over the asset’s useful life
descriptors.definition: The depreciable amount represents the cost or substituted valuation of an intangible asset minus its residual value. This amount is systematically allocated across the asset's determined useful life and typically recognized directly in profit or loss.
inclusion: Amortisation costs absorbed in producing other assets like inventories
nearby_distinctions: Depreciable amount calculation relies strictly on asset cost less residual value, distinct from gross carrying values.

descriptors.definition: Residual value is the estimated net disposal amount of an intangible asset at the end of its useful life. It is assumed to be zero unless a third-party commitment or active market reliably supports a higher expected recovery.
inclusion: Third-party commitments to purchase at useful life end
Active market-backed estimated disposal values
exclusion: Standard assumptions of terminal value without active market support
nearby_distinctions: Residual value adjusts the total depreciable base of the asset, separate from periodic impairment losses or amortisation method changes.

descriptors.definition: Amortisation commences when an intangible asset is available for use and ceases at the earlier of classification as held-for-sale or derecognition. The underlying amortisation period must be reviewed annually at each financial year-end to account for changed lifespan estimates.
inclusion: Assets in the location and condition necessary for intended operation
exclusion: Assets idled while still retaining active operational status
nearby_distinctions: Amortisation does not stop simply because an asset is idle, separating it from cessation triggers tied strictly to held-for-sale status or derecognition.

descriptors.definition: The chosen amortisation method must reflect the consumption pattern of the asset's future economic benefits, reverting to straight-line if that pattern is unreliable. A strict rebuttable presumption applies against revenue-based methods unless economic consumption directly correlates with revenue generation.
inclusion: Straight-line, diminishing balance, and units of production methods
exclusion: Revenue-based methods, unless strictly justified under exceptional presumptions
nearby_distinctions: Method selection focuses purely on benefit consumption patterns, which differs from determining the operational length of the amortisation period.

descriptors.concept_name: Intangible Assets With Indefinite Useful Lives
descriptors.definition: Assets with indefinite useful lives are exempt from periodic amortisation but must be tested for impairment annually or whenever indicators arise. Management must continuously review supporting circumstances each period to validate that the indefinite classification remains appropriate.
inclusion: Assets with no foreseeable limit to expected net cash inflows
exclusion: Assets with finite or determinable operational life windows
nearby_distinctions: Indefinite classification replaces systematic amortisation with rigorous annual impairment reviews, unlike finite assets.

descriptors.definition: Intangible asset impairment evaluation follows the framework outlined in Ind AS 36 to verify carrying amounts against recoverable amounts. Assets with indefinite useful lives must be evaluated for impairment at least on an annual basis.
inclusion: Annual reviews for indefinite-life assets
Event-driven impairment checks
nearby_distinctions: Impairment captures unexpected declines in service potential or value below carrying cost, distinct from scheduled periodic amortisation.

descriptors.definition: An intangible asset is derecognized upon disposal or when no future economic benefits are expected from its use or retirement. Gains or losses are computed as the difference between net disposal proceeds and the carrying amount, recognized directly in profit or loss.
inclusion: Disposals via sale, finance lease, or donation
Derecognition of replaced component parts
exclusion: Classification of gains as ordinary revenue
nearby_distinctions: Derecognition permanently removes the asset and isolates disposal gains/losses from operating revenue classifications.

descriptors.definition: Entities must provide comprehensive class-by-class disclosures for intangible assets, distinguishing between internally generated assets and other types. Required disclosures cover useful life assessments, amortisation methods, gross carrying balances, and full reconciliation statements of changes.
inclusion: Breakdowns of additions, disposals, and revaluations
Justifications for indefinite useful life assumptions
exclusion: Omission of class-level distinction between internal and external development
nearby_distinctions: Disclosure mandates structured reconciliations of opening to closing carrying amounts, extending beyond basic balance sheet presentations.

descriptors.concept_name: Extracts Of Financial Statements Of Listed Entity
descriptors.definition: Financial statement extracts illustrate practical corporate accounting policies, asset measurement rules, and footnote disclosures for intangible assets. They detail specific amortization parameters applied to technical know-how, software, and development rights.
inclusion: Practical company accounting policy disclosures
Applied amortisation schedules for specific asset categories
exclusion: Theoretical framework guidelines without empirical reporting context
nearby_distinctions: Financial extracts provide real-world application examples of standard accounting policies rather than setting new standard rules.
